Subject: Q3 renewal — priority response window and burst needs

Hi Nikhil,

As we approach our Q3 renewal, we'd like to discuss switching to a priority response SLA and reserving burst capacity for anticipated traffic spikes tied to an upcoming product launch. High-level ask: 99th-percentile response at <= 350ms for our production chat endpoints, and a burst pool that can handle an additional 20% peak throughput for two 48-hour windows per month.

I've attached our internal forecast and a short workbook with expected token volumes by service and week (Fjord_SLA_Request_Q3-2026.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can cover those latency targets under a dedicated lane or if we should consider a hybrid: dedicated for chat, hosted for background tasks?

We also want clarity on how the billing would work for sustained reserved capacity vs. burst credits, and whether there are minimum term commitments needed to lock in pricing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call this week.

Best,
Emma Li
Director of Platform
Fjord Analytics

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast workbook. We can support the priority response objective but I want to outline two practical paths so we can pick the one that matches Fjord's risk/tco profile:

Option A — Dedicated lane (recommended for latency guarantees)
- Dedicated GPU pool pinned to your model family
- 99th p95/p99 targets driven by instance sizing + continuous batching tuning
- Reserved capacity pricing (monthly) with discount at 12-month commit
- Separate burst buffer billed as monthly reserved burst credits (used during 48-hour windows)

Option B — Hybrid (lower commit, slightly higher tail latency risk)
- Dedicated capacity for chat (critical path), hosted for non-critical background workloads
- Auto-fallback to compatible quantized model when dedicated pool is saturated
- Burst handled by regional hosted pool with higher per-token rate

Attached: "SLA-Pricing-Q3-2026.pdf" with ballpark pricing scenarios for both options and an example amortized cost model. Highlights: to meet your 350ms 99th in the us-west region we estimate a dedicated mm-mirrored pool sized to handle 85% sustained plus the 20% burst buffer.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment here at Redwood on exact instance sizing and credit model — I'll loop in ops.
2) Confirm which option Fjord prefers so we can produce a formal amendment and pricing addendum.
3) If you want, we can schedule a technical alignment call (30m) with our performance engineer to review request traces and the forecast.

Are you available Fri 5/22 10:00–11:00 PT for a quick sync?

Thanks,
Nikhil
Account Executive — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
